claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
For a source-based plugin package, the package's version is the Git tag on the repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), whether or not it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected, and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed.
